data.content:
- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the

      "summary": "================================================================================
CURRENT STATE, READ THIS FIRST (review-ajcr r4, 2026-07-30). Everything below
this block is the audit HISTORY: five layers of correction and self-correction,
in which the actual costing does not appear until roughly halfway down. It is
kept because each retraction is evidence, but a lane picking a target should
read this block and then jump to the header "THE COSTING, RE-RANKED".

THE MACHINE IS SOUND AND HAS NOTHING TO FEED IT. pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy
(Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are sorry-free, kernel-confirmed, non-circular,
and WOULD produce a representing scheme. All three antecedents are undischarged
and no sorry-free witness exists for any of them.

THE THREE ANTECEDENTS, ranked by measured cost, cheapest last:
 1. IsChartUniv (the per-index chart certificate, `hf`) -- CERT-Sigma-gated.
    At V = top only the conditional theorem
    not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective is proved; its noninjectivity premise
    has no producer. At V = bot only some clauses are free, with no full datum
    inhabitant. Whether the PAIR holds at any concrete V remains open. Rows: chart-u, chart-restrict, atlas-coupling.
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc f (DAT-B coverage) -- the most
    expensive, and multi-round (told to the human as I-1090). Cannot be discounted
    by restricting the atlas: ajcr-p1's isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono carries
    any V up to top, where the inclusion is an iso. Restricted coverage is no
    cheaper than unrestricted -- and note only ONE direction is proved, so it is
    as measured STRICTLY STRONGER. Row: dat-b.
 3. rep i (a representation of the widened divFunctorAff at each parameter) -- the R2 divisor-
    representability target. Rows: ddr.divrep (+ u2, abel-widened); the old chart-typed divFunctor route is not the current carrier.

RIDERS THAT ARE NOT SEPARATE OBLIGATIONS, both established by retraction below:
 * hD (LocallyOfFiniteType) is a rider on antecedent 3, proved via
   rep.uniqueUpToIso -- unconditional, not contingent on the carrier divRep
   returns.
 * hcpt IS the JacobianData.quasiCompact field, so dat-glue and dat-j name ONE
   obligation. Qualification (r4, I-1162): the half carrying that -- the mpr
   direction -- has been the producer's own implementation since 07-27
   (JacobianDataCharts.lean:216); the new content is the mp direction, which
   shows the identification cannot be undone. hcl still has no producer, so
   nothing there is discharged.

r4 REPRICING -- WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHOR, same session. I wrote here that the chart
parameter n is pinned to the genus by chi_moduleKSheaf UNCONDITIONALLY, so
abel-noninj owed no "we are at n = g" argument and its n > g branch was
unreachable. FALSE, refuted by a fresh-context audit (I-1176) and reproduced:
chi_moduleKSheaf CONVERTS chi = 1 - n into n = genus C, it does not SUPPLY
chi = 1 - n. With n free and no chi hypothesis the goal FAILS, and it still fails
with a representation at n in scope. My probe had hchi as a binder, so it measured
the conversion (I-1177).
   THE STANDING PRICE is ajcr-p2's: n > g is unreachable for a chart built on a
producer IN THIS TREE, because each such producer carries an hchi at its own
index. That is a claim about producers and a lane must keep them in view.
Whether an inhabitant exists at n != genus C is an OPEN inhabitation question
about DivRepAffinePullback -- mixedParamChart typechecks at arbitrary nn.
abel-noninj's live target is unchanged: the carve question, does DivScheme g
contain points where H^1 fails to vanish.

*** hcpt CLAUSE RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), refuted by ajcr-p4 (I-1007)
within minutes of my writing it. THE DEGENERACY OBSERVATION IS REAL; MY CAUSAL READING WAS
CONFOUNDED. ***

I wrote, in the self-correction below, that "hcpt is NOT an independent gate but a CONSEQUENCE of
coverage", inferred from hcpt being free at iota := PEmpty while all content sat in the
IsLocallySurjective instance. p4's refutation is decisive and I verified its pivot myself (EXIT=0):
PEmpty IS FINITE. So freeness of hcpt there is explained by the FINITE-INDEX route
(JacobianData.ofCharts with per-chart compactness at an empty cover), with coverage contributing
nothing. A degenerate index attributes to whichever hypothesis happens to vary, and I varied the
wrong one.

WHAT p4 MEASURED, more useful than my claim was: feeding the openCover route directly,
(glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace fails on EXACTLY ONE goal --
Finite (glueData hf).openCover.I0. Not chart compactness, not the cover being a cover, not
coverage. Add [Finite iota] plus per-chart CompactSpace and the same term closes. p4 also applies my
own I-0978 correctly: a failing synthesis measures the instance graph, so this does NOT prove hcpt
independent of coverage -- it shows no route in scope derives it, and the single gap on the
available route is INDEX FINITENESS, which the class-indexed atlas provably lacks.

CONSEQUENCE, and it strengthens the item rather than weakening it: DO NOT schedule "derive hcpt
from coverage". The two honest options are the ones the tree names -- a finite atlas, or the Abel
image (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage out of a quasi-compact DivScheme). The class-indexed atlas
needs the second, and PRICING IT is the unowned work. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j points there.

`k` — which is the separatedness half of Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1): the
relative Picard presheaf is a separated presheaf for the étale topology, so its
sheafification (the one-step plus `PicEtAff`) has an injective unit. The assembly follows
the "Refined design" of `informal/c1-etale-separatedness-assembly.md` (the ζ-decomposition
of the scheme-side step ε3/ζ), consuming brick 3 (`Over.prPullback_injective`), the
projection-descent equivalence (ε1, `Picard/ProjectionUnits.lean`), the composite unit
descent (ε2, `Descent/UnitDescentComposite.lean`) and the dictionary naturality (γ,
`Picard/CechPicToPicNaturality.lean`).

## What is landed here (ζ1)

`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.cechPicMap_tensorInl_eq_tensorInr`, the **class-level coherence
seed**: if a Čech Picard class `L` on the curve-product `C ⊗ Spec A` restricts, over a test
algebra `A → B`, to something pulled back from the base — i.e. `p_B^* N = (C ◁ Spec f)^* L`
for `N : CechPic (Spec B)` and `f = ofId A B` — then the two base changes of `N` to
`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` agree along the two coprojections `tensorInl, tensorInr : B →ₐ[k] B ⊗[A] B`.

(`Scheme.CechPic.map_comp` + `Over.snd_left_naturality` + `Over.overSpecMap_comp`), and
pullback along the curve projection is injective (brick 3), so they are equal. This is the
"one genuinely delicate step" reduced to its cocycle-free seed — the honest descent datum is
built downstream (ζ2).

    "content": "noncomputable def descendedCollapseEquiv {v : (P ⊗[A] P)ˣ} (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) :
    (B ⊗[A] hv.descended) ≃ₗ[B] (hv.collapse (B := B)).descended := by
  refine (DescentDatum.ofUnit _ (hv.collapse (B := B))).equivDescended
    (N := B ⊗[A] hv.descended)
    ((AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B P P hv.descended).trans
      (DescentDatum.ofUnit v hv).descentEquiv)
    fun x => ?_
  induction x with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul b' w =>
      induction w with
      | zero => simp
      | tmul b m =>
          have h : tensorCollapse A B P v.val * ((m : P) ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : P))
              = 1 ⊗ₜ[B] (m : P) := by
            have := congrArg (tensorCollapse A B P) (hv.mem_descended.mp m.2)
            rwa [map_mul, tensorCollapse_tmul, tensorCollapse_tmul] at this
          simp only [LinearEquiv.trans_apply, AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul,
            ofUnit_coaction, unitCoaction_apply,
            DescentDatum.baseChange_coaction, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul,
            LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, TensorProduct.mk_apply]
          change tensorCollapse A B P v.val * (((b • b') • (m : P)) ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : P))
              = b' ⊗ₜ[B] ((b • (1 : P)) • (m : P))
          simp only [smul_eq_mul]
          rw [show (b • (1 : P)) * (m : P) = b • (m : P) by rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul]]
          rw [show ((b • b') * (m : P)) ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : P)
                = ((b • b') ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : P)) * ((m : P) ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : P)) by
              rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one]]
          rw [show b' ⊗ₜ[B] (b • (m : P))
                = ((b • b') ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : P)) * ((1 : P) ⊗ₜ[B] (m : P)) by
              rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one, one_mul, ← smul_tmul]]
          linear_combination ((b • b') ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : P)) * h
      | add x y hx hy =>
          simp only [tmul_add, map_add] at hx hy ⊢
          rw [hx, hy]

  -- on pure tensors to the ring computation

  --   = (b ⊗ₜ 1) * (1 ⊗ₜ m) * (1 ⊗ₜ n) = b ⊗ₜ (m*n)`

    (N := hu.descended ⊗[A] hv.descended) (descendedMulAux hu hv) fun x => ?_
